pillarOverview.title: Education, Employability & Industry Readiness
pillarOverview.tagline: Bridging Academic Preparation and Professional Software Engineering
pillarOverview.description: We partner with engineering colleges, placement officers, and faculty to deliver structured, human-evaluated assessments and immersive delivery simulations. We emphasize transparent feedback, grounded expectations, and genuine competence over hype.
pillarOverview.humanLedCommitment: Our employability assessments are led and reviewed by experienced human evaluators. AI assists solely in aggregating patterns and formatting summary reports. We do not use automated black-box scoring to replace human engineering judgment, and we never make false promises of guaranteed placements.

services.name: Comprehensive Employability Assessment
services.shortDescription: Supervised paper-based and practical evaluations covering 18 foundational software engineering competencies, followed by 1-on-1 human technical interviews.
services.fullDescription: A multi-dimensional diagnostic process designed to give students and institutions a clear, unvarnished picture of technical and problem-solving readiness. Unlike automated multiple-choice tests that reward rote memorization, our assessment combines supervised evaluations with individual technical interviews conducted by seasoned engineers.
businessProblem: High GPA students frequently struggle in live technical interviews due to superficial conceptual understanding.
Online automated coding platforms reward memorization of solutions rather than structured problem-solving and communication.
Colleges lack granular diagnostic data showing exactly where curriculum coverage diverges from industry expectations.
Students lack practice articulating technical tradeoffs, architecture choices, and project code under interview pressure.
synezaSolution: Multi-topic diagnostic covering programming fundamentals, OOP, data structures, databases, networking, OS, and APIs.
Human-led individual technical interviews assessing thought process, problem decomposition, and code clarity.
Institutional skill-gap reporting mapping student cohort performance against core industry competency standards.
Actionable student feedback detailing specific focus areas for remediation prior to formal campus recruitment.
keyCapabilities: Supervised paper-based and written programming assessments
Aptitude, logical reasoning, and algorithmic problem-solving
Core CS evaluations: Data Structures, OOP, OS, Networks, Computer Architecture
Databases, SQL queries, and transaction understanding
Software engineering discipline: Testing, Version Control (Git), REST APIs
Final-year project deep-dive and technical communication assessment
One-on-one structured interviews with engineering practitioners

services.name: Software Company Simulation
services.shortDescription: A 2-day practical Agile software delivery simulation featuring 4 sprints, prepared user stories, change requests, and a working proof-of-concept demonstration.
services.fullDescription: The Software Company Simulation places engineering students inside a realistic delivery environment designed to simulate a working engineering squad. Over 17 structured hours (1 hour of Agile immersion followed by four 4-hour sprints), student teams take realistic user stories with acceptance criteria, manage backlogs, respond to mid-project change requests, and build a verified working proof of concept.
targetAudience: Colleges seeking hands-on industry exposure for students
businessProblem: Graduating engineers have never worked with team-based version control branches, pull requests, or merge conflicts.
Academic projects rarely include formal acceptance criteria, peer code reviews, or automated unit tests.
Students have never experienced the reality of sudden client change requests or sprint timeboxing.
Isolated coding exercises fail to teach collaborative architecture, documentation, and sprint demonstrations.
synezaSolution: A fully prepared simulated enterprise scenario with backlog, user stories, and acceptance test definitions.
17 intensive hours structured into four 4-hour sprints plus Agile fundamentals immersion.
Deliberate injection of a scope change request in Sprint 3 to evaluate adaptive engineering and teamwork.
Final sprint proof-of-concept demonstration evaluated against defined acceptance criteria and code hygiene.
keyCapabilities: Four 4-hour delivery sprints (16 hours sprint time + 1 hour Agile kickoff = 17 hours total)
Backlog grooming, user story sizing, and sprint commitment
Git branch management, feature branches, and pull request reviews
Automated testing fundamentals and integration checks
Handling mid-sprint requirement change requests under realistic constraints
Executive proof-of-concept presentation and technical walkthrough

simulationDetails.title: Software Company Simulation: Detailed 17-Hour Structure

structure.title: Practical Agile Immersion
activities: Overview of Agile vs. Waterfall in real enterprise environments
Role definition: Product Owner, Scrum Master, Lead Engineer, QA
Examining the project charter, user story anatomy, and acceptance criteria
Local development environment setup and Git remote branch cloning

structure.title: Sprint 1: Foundation & Baseline Stories
activities: Sprint planning meeting and story point estimation
Creating domain models, database schema definitions, and migration scripts
Implementing initial REST endpoints or core service interfaces
Authoring unit tests for baseline business logic
End-of-sprint standup and review against initial acceptance criteria

structure.title: Sprint 2: Feature Expansion & Collaborative Integration
activities: Branching strategy execution: feature branches and pull requests
Resolving first real Git merge conflicts among team members
Building operational business workflows and error handling
Integration testing between API layer and persistence layer
Peer code reviews focusing on readability, edge cases, and logging

structure.title: Sprint 3: The Change Request & Agile Adaptation
activities: Introduction of an unexpected simulated customer change request
Assessing blast radius of change on existing schema and API contracts
Refactoring existing modules without breaking previously passed tests
Team trade-off negotiation: what stays in scope vs. what gets deprioritized
Updating regression tests and continuous integration checks

structure.title: Sprint 4: Verification, Demo & Retrospective
activities: Bug bashing and edge-case testing under time constraints
Preparing release notes and architectural proof-of-concept summary
Formal sprint review: demonstrating the working application to evaluators
Sprint retrospective: what went well, communication breakdowns, and lessons learned
Individual feedback debrief on teamwork and engineering habits

learningOutcomes: Grasps what a daily software engineering workflow actually feels like before graduation.
Understands how to decompose user stories and write code that satisfies explicit acceptance criteria.
Experiences the reality of handling merge conflicts, pull request feedback, and mid-course change requests.
Gains concrete experiences and anecdotes to discuss authentically during technical interviews.
